title: Push width further: ASPECT_RATIO 80->112 (model_dim 896)
description: Increased ASPECT_RATIO from 80 to 112 (model_dim 640->896, 7 heads) at DEPTH=8, and preemptively lowered DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE from 128 to 64 to stay under the VRAM ceiling (grad_accum_steps auto-adjusted 2->4). Deliberately went further than the crowd's ASPECT_RATIO=96 proposal to bracket the width-scaling trend rather than duplicate it, since all 6 agents independently proposed the identical 96 config this round.
reflection: val_bpb 1.037256 - clearly worse than the current baseline (0.999094) and even worse than the pre-width-scaling baseline (1.012413). The width-scaling win does NOT continue monotonically to model_dim=896; it reverses sharply. Peak VRAM was only 38.8GB (well under ceiling), confirming VRAM was not the binding constraint here - something about this width/batch combination hurts optimization. Caveat: I changed both ASPECT_RATIO and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE simultaneously (128->64, doubling grad_accum_steps 2->4), which is a confound - it's not a clean isolation of width alone, since doubling grad_accum steps could itself hurt convergence at fixed wall-clock (fewer total tokens processed per step, more Python/kernel-launch overhead per optimizer step, only 419 steps completed vs higher step counts at dim=640/batch=128). So this result should be read as 'model_dim=896 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=64 is bad', not necessarily 'model_dim=896 is bad' - a cleaner follow-up would test dim=896 at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128 if VRAM allows, or test the ASPECT_RATIO=96 config (which several of us proposed) at DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=64 to isolate whether the batch-size drop alone is the culprit. Given this result, I'd guess the width-scaling optimum is somewhere between 640 and 896, likely close to 768 (the crowd's ASPECT_RATIO=96 pick), and pushing much further starts to hurt - possibly because larger models need more warmup/tuning that a fixed 5-minute budget with fixed LR schedule doesn't provide, or because DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=64 with grad_accum=4 meaningfully hurts throughput/MFU at this model size.
